# Cursor IDE config and workflow

_**User**_

@zsh (1-197) let's make sense of both directories:

/Users/me/dotfiles/cursor
/Users/me/.cursor

one is a live cursor config directory for the running application, the other is a dotfiles repo for tracking configurations files, but it's not live, thought it might symlink to some live things.

there's a lot of old crufty stuff in here, but that's okay, we just need to figure out how to manage it.

and, I bet there are open source tools that can help if we search github, so let's understand the intent for what's here (including recognizing that the cursor subdir in the dotfiles dir is part of a larger repo of non-cursor things).

One more bit of context is that I'm constructing a repo for managing the bootrapping and configuration of tools and config files in this project directory:

/Users/me/tools/toolchain-2026
@zsh (3-55) 

which has a lot of different ideas that I'm trying out on a completely separate "sidequest" laptop where I can experiment and test things out, so let's look to this directory and its subdirs and many repos as a way to help us explore the current cursor situation on this mac laptop (which I'm calling "workhorse" to distinguish it from the other mac laptop "sidequest") 

so for this plan, let's understand the various intents across this dirs and repos, let's do some sensemaking of not only what's here, but also where we might want to go, and for our purposes we'll first just focus on the narrower, but very important, scope of the cursor IDE and its ecosystems of extensions and tools and utilitites so we can really highly focus our workflow and config management and toolchain orchestration for our live development workflow with "cursor at the center as our chef's knife" because if its versatility, utility, and primary UI for the devx (developer experience) as well as for any day-to-day interactions with llm and code and deployment and management.

All tests passed!'`\n\n### EXAMPLES\n\nBad (causes dquote> prompt in zsh):\n```bash\necho \"Fixed CLIENT_DOMAIN redirect issue!\"\necho \"✅ All tests passed!\"\n```\n\nGood (works in all shells):\n```bash\necho \"Fixed CLIENT_DOMAIN redirect issue\"\necho \"Fixed CLIENT_DOMAIN redirect issue.\"\necho 'Fixed CLIENT_DOMAIN redirect issue!'\necho \"✅ All tests passed\"\nprintf '%s\\n' \"Fixed CLIENT_DOMAIN redirect issue!\"\n```\n\n### WHY THIS MATTERS\n- In zsh, `!` inside double quotes triggers history expansion\n- This causes the shell to wait for more input, showing `dquote>` prompt\n- Users must manually type `\"` to continue, breaking automation\n- Single quotes or avoiding `!` entirely prevents this issue\n\n### GENERAL BEST PRACTICES\n- Prefer single quotes for literal strings with special characters\n- Use `printf '%s\\n' \"...\"` for complex strings\n- Keep echo messages professional without unnecessary punctuation\n- Avoid emoji + exclamation combinations like `\"✅ Done!\"`","isFromGlob":true,"alwaysApply":false}]}

{"contents":"# Cursor Workspace Snapshot Tools\n\nA comprehensive set of tools to capture and analyze your Cursor editor workspace state.\n\n## Overview\n\nThese scripts help you:\n- **Snapshot** all open windows, files, folders, and extensions\n- **Track** workspace history over time\n- **Compare** snapshots to see what changed\n- **Restore** context by reviewing past workspace states\n\n## Quick Start\n\n```bash\n# Create a snapshot\n./dump-cursor-windows.sh\n\n# View available snapshots\n./view-cursor-snapshots.sh list\n\n# View windows from latest snapshot\n./view-cursor-snapshots.sh windows latest\n```\n\n## Installation\n\n```bash\n# Optional but recommended for better output\nbrew install jq\n```\n\n## Tools\n\n### `dump-cursor-windows.sh`\n\nCreates a timestamped snapshot of your Cursor workspace.\n\n**Creates 3 files:**\n1. `cursor-workspace-YYYY-MM-DD_HH-MM-SS.txt` - Full `cursor --status` output\n2. `cursor-workspace-YYYY-MM-DD_HH-MM-SS.json` - Structured data extract\n3. `cursor-workspace-YYYY-MM-DD_HH-MM-SS-extensions.txt` - Installed extensions\n\n**Captures:**\n- All open windows with their current files\n- Workspace folders and paths\n- Recent files from menu\n- Workspace file statistics (file types, counts)\n- Workspace storage mappings\n- Extension list with versions\n\n**Usage:**\n```bash\n./dump-cursor-windows.sh\n```\n\n### `view-cursor-snapshots.sh`\n\nInteractive tool to explore and compare snapshots.\n\n**Commands:**\n\n```bash\n# List all snapshots\n./view-cursor-snapshots.sh list\n\n# View full snapshot data\n./view-cursor-snapshots.sh view N\n\n# List all open windows (showing current file + workspace)\n./view-cursor-snapshots.sh windows N\n\n# List tracked folders\n./view-cursor-snapshots.sh folders N\n\n# List recent files\n./view-cursor-snapshots.sh recent N\n\n# Show workspace statistics\n./view-cursor-snapshots.sh stats N\n\n# Compare two snapshots\n./view-cursor-snapshots.sh diff N1 N2\n\n# View latest snapshot\n./view-cursor-snapshots.sh latest\n```\n\n## JSON Structure\n\nThe `.json` files contain:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"timestamp\": \"2025-10-29_17-48-12\",\n  \"windows\": [\n    {\n      \"window_number\": 1,\n      \"workspace\": \"traub-umpire-empire\",\n      \"current_file\": \"officialspay_export_2025-09-29.json\"\n    }\n  ],\n  \"folders\": [\n    \"/Users/me/projects/traub-umpire-empire\",\n    \"/Users/me/tools/markdown-slides\"\n  ],\n  \"recent_files\": [\n    \"/Users/me/projects/dgx-spark/README.md\"\n  ],\n  \"workspace_stats\": {\n    \"cursor\": \"22 files\",\n    \"gcloud-default-1234\": \"17 files\"\n  },\n  \"workspace_files\": {\n    \"cursor\": {\n      \"path\": \"/Users/me/dotfiles/cursor\",\n      \"storage_id\": \"ad8316de0edfff49cfd059d4dfd6caf2\"\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n## Use Cases\n\n### 1. Daily Snapshots\n```bash\n# Add to your daily routine (e.g., via crontab or Alfred workflow)\ncd ~/dotfiles/cursor && ./dump-cursor-windows.sh\n```\n\n### 2. Before/After Comparisons\n```bash\n# Take snapshot before major refactoring\n./dump-cursor-windows.sh\n\n# Do your work...\n\n# Take another snapshot\n./dump-cursor-windows.sh\n\n# Compare\n./view-cursor-snapshots.sh diff 1 2\n```\n\n### 3. Context Recovery\n```bash\n# \"What was I working on last Tuesday?\"\n./view-cursor-snapshots.sh windows 5\n```\n\n### 4. Extension Audits\n```bash\n# Track extension changes over time\ndiff cursor-workspace-2025-10-01_*-extensions.txt \\\n     cursor-workspace-2025-10-29_*-extensions.txt\n```\n\n## Advanced Usage\n\n### Filtering with jq\n\n```bash\n# Get all workspaces\njq -r '.windows[].workspace' cursor-workspace-*.json | sort -u\n\n# Count windows per workspace\njq -r '.windows[] | .workspace' cursor-workspace-*.json | \\\n  sort | uniq -c | sort -rn\n\n# Find all markdown files\njq -r '.recent_files[] | select(endswith(\".md\"))' cursor-workspace-*.json\n\n# Get workspaces with most files\njq -r '.workspace_stats | to_entries[] | \n  \"\\(.key): \\(.value)\"' cursor-workspace-*.json | \\\n  grep -o '[0-9]* files' | sort -rn\n```\n\n### Automated Backups\n\n```bash\n# Archive old snapshots\nmkdir -p archives/$(date +%Y-%m)\nmv cursor-workspace-*.{txt,json} archives/$(date +%Y-%m)/\n```\n\n## Data Sources\n\nThe scripts extract data from:\n1. `cursor --status` - Process info, windows, workspace stats\n2. `~/Library/Application Support/Cursor/User/globalStorage/storage.json` - Folder list, recent files\n3. `~/Library/Application Support/Cursor/User/workspaceStorage/*/workspace.json` - Workspace mappings\n4. `cursor --list-extensions` - Extension inventory\n\n## Tips\n\n- Use `jq` for powerful JSON querying\n- Snapshots are plain text - they compress well with `gzip`\n- Compare `.json` files programmatically for automation\n- The `.txt` files contain raw process information useful for debugging\n\n## Troubleshooting\n\n**\"No snapshots found\"**\n- Run `./dump-cursor-windows.sh` first to create a snapshot\n\n**\"jq not installed\"**\n- Install with `brew install jq` for enhanced features\n- Scripts work without jq but with limited functionality\n\n**Empty or missing data**\n- Ensure Cursor is running when taking snapshot\n- Check that paths in script match your system\n\n## File Locations\n\nAll snapshots are stored in the same directory as the scripts:\n- Default: `~/dotfiles/cursor/`\n- Customize by editing `output_dir` in `dump-cursor-windows.sh`\n","numCharactersInRequestedRange":5096,"totalLinesInFile":220,"matchingCursorRules":[{"name":"derived-cursor-rules","body":"## PROJECT OVERVIEW\n\n## CODE STYLE\n\n## FOLDER ORGANIZATION\n\n## TECH STACK\n- Node.js (for scripts)\n- Python (for scripts)\n- TypeScript (for scripts)\n- JavaScript (for scripts)\n- Go (for scripts)\n- R (for scripts)\n- Shell (for scripts)\n- @modelcontextprotocol/server-github\n- @modelcontextprotocol/server-git\n- @modelcontextprotocol/server-gitlab\n\n## PROJECT-SPECIFIC STANDARDS\n\n## WORKFLOW & RELEASE RULES\n- Restart Cursor completely after making configuration changes. All tests passed!'`\n\n### EXAMPLES\n\nBad (causes dquote> prompt in zsh):\n```bash\necho \"Fixed CLIENT_DOMAIN redirect issue!\"\necho \"✅ All tests passed!\"\n```\n\nGood (works in all shells):\n```bash\necho \"Fixed CLIENT_DOMAIN redirect issue\"\necho \"Fixed CLIENT_DOMAIN redirect issue.\"\necho 'Fixed CLIENT_DOMAIN redirect issue!'\necho \"✅ All tests passed\"\nprintf '%s\\n' \"Fixed CLIENT_DOMAIN redirect issue!\"\n```\n\n### WHY THIS MATTERS\n- In zsh, `!` inside double quotes triggers history expansion\n- This causes the shell to wait for more input, showing `dquote>` prompt\n- Users must manually type `\"` to continue, breaking automation\n- Single quotes or avoiding `!` entirely prevents this issue\n\n### GENERAL BEST PRACTICES\n- Prefer single quotes for literal strings with special characters\n- Use `printf '%s\\n' \"...\"` for complex strings\n- Keep echo messages professional without unnecessary punctuation\n- Avoid emoji + exclamation combinations like `\"✅ Done!\"`","isFromGlob":true,"alwaysApply":false}]}

{"contents":"# macOS 2026 Toolchain\n\nA Spacemacs-style layered approach to reproducible macOS development environment configuration.\n\n## Quick Start\n\n### Bootstrap from GitHub (No Git Required)\n\nOn a fresh macOS system where git isn't available yet (git requires Xcode Command Line Tools), you can bootstrap directly from GitHub using curl:\n\n```bash\n# Download and run bootstrap script (recommended - safer)\ncurl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aculich/toolchain-2026/main/bootstrap.sh -o /tmp/bootstrap.sh && chmod +x /tmp/bootstrap.sh && /tmp/bootstrap.sh\n```\n\nOr as a one-liner (pipes directly to bash):\n\n```bash\ncurl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aculich/toolchain-2026/main/bootstrap.sh | bash\n```\n\n**Note**: This is useful for fresh macOS installations where git isn't installed yet. After bootstrap completes, you'll have git and can clone the repository normally.\n\n### Standard Quick Start (Git Already Available)\n\nIf you already have git installed:\n\n```bash\n# Clone the repository\ngit clone https://github.com/aculich/toolchain-2026.git\ncd toolchain-2026\n\n# Quick start with script-based (default)\n./bootstrap.sh\n./install.sh --base\n\n# Or choose Nix-based installation\n./bootstrap.sh --install-method nix\ncd nixos-config && ./install-lix-complete.sh\n\n# Or choose Pixi-based installation (fastest, best for data science)\n./bootstrap.sh --install-method pixi\n./install-pixi.sh --base --data\n\n# Install base + AI development\n./install.sh --base --ai\n\n# Install everything\n./install.sh --all\n\n# See all options\n./install.sh --help\n```\n\n**Note**: Three installation approaches are available:\n- **Script-based** (default): Homebrew-based, fast, native macOS integration\n- **Nix-based**: Fully declarative, reproducible, system configuration\n- **Pixi-based** (new): Fastest setup, excellent for data science, hybrid approach\n\nSee [docs/PIXI_VS_SCRIPT_VS_NIX.md](docs/PIXI_VS_SCRIPT_VS_NIX.md) for comparison. Decision deadline: Mid-February 2026.\n\n## Hard Reset (Fresh Start)\n\n**Purpose**: Remove Nix partition and user data to start completely fresh without reinstalling macOS.\n\n**What gets removed**:\n- Nix store (`/nix`)\n- User home directory contents\n- Homebrew packages (if desired)\n- All local repositories\n\n**What's preserved**: macOS installation, system files, other user accounts\n\n### Hard Reset Process\n\n1. **Remove Nix Installation** (if installed):\n   ```bash\n   # If installed with Lix\n   /nix/nix-installer uninstall\n   \n   # Or manually remove Nix\n   sudo rm -rf /nix\n   sudo rm -rf /etc/nix\n   sudo rm -rf ~/.config/nix\n   sudo rm -rf ~/.nix-profile\n   sudo rm -rf ~/.nix-defexpr\n   # Remove Nix references from shell profiles (~/.zshrc, ~/.bash_profile)\n   ```\n\n2. **Remove User Data** (choose one method):\n   - **Method A - Recovery Mode** (most thorough):\n     - Boot to Recovery Mode (Apple Silicon: hold power; Intel: Cmd+R)\n     - Open Terminal\n     - `rm -rf /Users/username/*`\n     - Reboot\n   - **Method B - Multi-User** (recommended for frequent resets):\n     - Log into another admin account\n     - Delete user account via System Preferences\n     - Recreate user account\n\n3. **Clean Up Homebrew** (optional):\n   ```bash\n   /bin/bash -c \"$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Homebrew/install/HEAD/uninstall.sh)\"\n   ```\n\n## Complete Setup from Scratch\n\nAfter a hard reset or on a fresh macOS installation, follow these steps to set up your development environment.\n\n### Phase 1: Clone Repository\n\n```bash\ncd ~\ngit clone https://github.com/aculich/toolchain-2026.git\ncd toolchain-2026\n```\n\n### Phase 2: Bootstrap\n\n```bash\n./bootstrap.sh\n# Or choose installation method:\n./bootstrap.sh --install-method nix    # Use Nix-based\n./bootstrap.sh --install-method script # Use script-based (default)\n./bootstrap.sh --install-method ask   # Interactive choice\n\n# If interrupted, resume from checkpoint:\n./bootstrap.sh --resume\n```\n\n**What bootstrap installs**:\n- Xcode Command Line Tools\n- Homebrew\n- bash 4+, git, GNU tools\n- Cursor, 1Password CLI, llm CLI\n\n**New features** (2026-01-04):\n- **Comprehensive logging** - All operations logged with timestamps\n- **Checkpoint system** - Resume from any checkpoint with `--resume`\n- **Early Touch ID setup** - Enables Touch ID for sudo before any sudo operations\n- **Enhanced 1Password setup** - Interactive guide with guard system\n- **Sentinel monitoring** - Real-time monitoring with error detection\n- **Progress reporting** - Visual progress bars and step announcements\n\n**Manual steps during bootstrap**:\n1. Install Xcode Command Line Tools (if prompted)\n2. Sign in to 1Password CLI: `op signin`\n\n### Phase 3: Configure 1Password\n\n**Set up GitHub plugin**:\n```bash\nop plugin init gh\n# Follow prompts to select/create GitHub credentials item\n# Choose scope (global recommended)\n\n# Source plugin\nsource ~/.config/op/plugins.sh\n\n# Add to shell profile for persistence\necho 'source ~/.config/op/plugins.sh' >> ~/.zshrc\n```\n\n**Authenticate GitHub CLI**:\n```bash\ngh auth login\n# Will use 1Password for authentication\n```\n\n**Verify**:\n```bash\ngh auth status\nop plugin inspect gh\n```\n\n### Phase 4: Clone Companion Repositories\n\n**Public repos** (automatically cloned by bootstrap):\n- `devx-companion-2026`\n- `outer-world-context-2026`\n- `data-public-2026`\n\n**Private repos** (manual, after 1Password setup):\n```bash\ncd ~\ngh repo clone aculich/data-private-2026\ngh repo clone aculich/nix-secrets\n```\n\n### Phase 5: Set Up Touch ID for Sudo\n\n```bash\ncd ~/toolchain-2026\n./scripts/enable-touchid-sudo.sh\n```\n\n**What it does**:\n- Adds Touch ID authentication to `/etc/pam.d/sudo`\n- Enables fingerprint authentication for sudo commands\n- Creates backup of original sudo config\n\n**Test**:\n```bash\nsudo ls /var/root\n# Should prompt for Touch ID instead of password\n```\n\n### Phase 6: Configure macOS Keychain Passkeys\n\n**Enable iCloud Keychain** (if desired):\n- System Settings → Apple ID → iCloud\n- Enable \"Passwords and Keychain\"\n\n**1Password can also manage passkeys**:\n- Already configured via 1Password CLI integration\n- Passkeys stored in 1Password vault\n\n### Phase 7: Install Development Environment\n\n**Option A - Script-Based** (default):\n```bash\ncd ~/toolchain-2026\n./install.sh --base --ai --macos\n```\n\n**Option B - Nix-Based**:\n```bash\ncd ~/toolchain-2026/nixos-config\n./install-lix-complete.sh\n# After installation:\nnix run '.#build-switch'\n```\n\n**What gets installed**:\n- Shell tools (zsh, starship, fzf, bat)\n- Version managers (mise)\n- Development tools (direnv, git-delta)\n- Essential macOS apps\n- Nix system (if using Nix-based)\n\n### Phase 8: Set Up Nix Secrets (if using Nix)\n\n```bash\ncd ~/toolchain-2026/nixos-config\n\n# Apply configuration (will prompt for secrets repo path)\nnix run .#apply\n\n# Or manually configure secrets repository\n# Edit flake.nix to point to your nix-secrets repo\n```\n\n**Secrets repository structure**:\n- `nix-secrets/secrets.nix` - Defines which keys can decrypt secrets\n- `nix-secrets/*.age` - Encrypted secrets files\n\n### Phase 9: Post-Install Verification\n\n```bash\ncd ~/toolchain-2026/nixos-config\n./scripts/post-install-verify.sh\n```\n\n**Verifies**:\n- Nix installation (if used)\n- Packages installed\n- Homebrew integration\n- System state\n- Fixes common issues (zsh completion, app quarantine)\n\n## Layers\n\n| Layer | Name | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| 0 | **Base** | Core CLI tools, shell config, mise, 1Password, fonts |\n| 1 | **AI** | Cursor, Warp, Ollama, MCP servers, AI assistants |\n| 2 | **Web** | uv, Node.js, browsers, API tools, databases |\n| 3 | **Data** | Pixi, R, Jupyter, scientific computing |\n| 4 | **Cloud** | Docker/OrbStack, GCP, Firebase, Kubernetes, Terraform |\n| 5 | **Mobile** | Xcode, Android Studio, Flutter, React Native, fastlane |\n| **MCP** | **MCP Base** | MCP dependencies, Repomix (see [MCP Layer Guide](docs/MCP_LAYER_GUIDE.md)) |\n\n## Directory Structure\n\n```\ntoolchain-2026/\n├── install.sh              # Main installer\n├── Brewfile.base           # Layer 0: Base tools\n├── Brewfile.ai             # Layer 1: AI development\n├── Brewfile.web            # Layer 2: Web development\n├── Brewfile.data           # Layer 3: Data science\n├── Brewfile.cloud          # Layer 4: Cloud/DevOps\n├── Brewfile.mobile         # Layer 5: Mobile development\n├── shell/                  # Shell configuration\n│   ├── env.sh              # Shared env (zsh + bash)\n│   ├── .zshrc.template     # Template for ~/.zshrc\n│   └── .zshrc.d/           # Modular zsh configs\n├── templates/              # Project templates\n│   ├── python-project/     # uv-based Python\n│   ├── node-project/       # TypeScript Node.js\n│   ├── flutter-project/    # Flutter mobile\n│   ├── react-native-project/\n│   └── datascience-project/\n├── upstream/               # Curated reference repos\n│   ├── SOURCES.md          # List of repos\n│   └── sync.sh             # Clone/update script\n├── mcp/                    # MCP configuration\n│   ├── mcp-config.json     # Server definitions template\n│   └── docker-compose/      # Docker Compose templates for MCP servers\n├── secrets/                # Secrets management docs\n│   └── README.md           # Strategy & patterns\n└── docs/\n    └── SYLLABUS.md         # Learning path\n```\n\n## Usage\n\n### Install Layers\n\n```bash\n# List available layers\n./install.sh --list\n\n# Install base only\n./install.sh --base\n\n# Install multiple layers\n./install.sh --base --ai --web\n\n# Add a layer later\n./install.sh --add cloud\n```\n\n### Configure Shell\n\n```bash\n# Apply shell configuration\n./install.sh --configure-shell\n\n# Or manually source in ~/.zshrc:\n# TOOLCHAIN_DIR=\"$HOME/.config/toolchain-2026\"\n# for config in \"$TOOLCHAIN_DIR/shell/.zshrc.d\"/*.zsh(N); do\n#     source \"$config\"\n# done\n```\n\n### Sync Upstream Repos\n\n```bash\n# Clone all reference repositories\n./upstream/sync.sh\n\n# Sync specific category\n./upstream/sync.sh --category dotfiles\n./upstream/sync.sh --category ai-tooling\n```\n\n### Use Project Templates\n\n```bash\n# Copy template to new project\ncp -r templates/python-project ~/projects/my-new-app\ncd ~/projects/my-new-app\nuv sync\n```\n\n## Key Tools by Layer\n\n### Layer 0: Base\n\n- **mise** - Runtime version manager (Python, Node, Rust, etc.)\n- **direnv** - Directory-specific environment variables\n- **1password-cli** - Biometric secrets injection\n- **starship** - Cross-shell prompt\n- **fzf, ripgrep, bat, eza** - Modern CLI tools\n\n### Layer 1: AI\n\n- **Cursor** - AI-native code editor\n- **Warp** - AI-powered terminal\n- **Ollama** - Local LLM runner\n- **MCP** - Model Context Protocol servers (see [MCP Quick Start](docs/MCP_QUICK_START.md))\n\n### Layer 2: Web\n\n- **uv** - Fast Python package manager\n- **pnpm** - Fast Node.js package manager\n- **TablePlus** - Database GUI\n- **httpie** - HTTP client\n\n### Layer 3: Data\n\n- **Pixi** - conda-forge with lockfiles\n- **R + RStudio** - Statistical computing\n- **DuckDB** - Analytical database\n\n### Layer 4: Cloud\n\n- **OrbStack** - Fast Docker runtime\n- **gcloud** - Google Cloud CLI\n- **kubectl, k9s** - Kubernetes tools\n- **Terraform** - Infrastructure as code\n\n### Layer 5: Mobile\n\n- **Xcode** - iOS development\n- **Android Studio** - Android development\n- **Flutter** - Cross-platform framework\n- **fastlane** - Mobile CI/CD automation\n\n## Secrets Management\n\nAll secrets flow through 1Password. Never store plaintext secrets.\n\n```bash\n# .envrc example\nexport API_KEY=$(op read \"op://Development/MyAPI/api_key\")\n\n# Run with secrets\nop run -- python my_app.py\nop run -- docker compose up\n```\n\nSee [secrets/README.md](secrets/README.md) for the complete strategy.\n\n## Learning Path\n\nFollow [docs/SYLLABUS.md](docs/SYLLABUS.md) for a structured learning path through each layer.\n\n## Customization\n\n1. Fork this repository\n2. Edit Brewfiles to add/remove packages\n3. Customize shell configs in `shell/.zshrc.d/`\n4. Add your own templates\n5. Update `upstream/SOURCES.md` with repos you find useful\n\n## Philosophy\n\n- **Layered** - Start minimal, add what you need\n- **Reproducible** - Brewfiles + lockfiles everywhere\n- **Secure** - 1Password references, never plaintext secrets\n- **Learnable** - Upstream repos for best practices\n- **Future-ready** - Nix/Devbox paths preserved for later adoption\n\n## Troubleshooting\n\n### 1Password not authenticated\n\n```bash\nop signin\n```\n\n### GitHub authentication fails\n\n```bash\ngh auth status\nop plugin inspect gh\ngh auth login  # Re-authenticate\n```\n\n### Touch ID not working for sudo\n\n```bash\n./scripts/enable-touchid-sudo.sh\n# May need to re-run after macOS updates\n```\n\n### Nix packages not in PATH\n\n```bash\nsource ~/.nix-profile/etc/profile.d/nix.sh\n# Or restart terminal\n```\n\n### Apps quarantined after install\n\n```bash\n./scripts/remove-quarantine.sh\n```\n\n## Related Documentation\n\n- [docs/TESTING_PLAN.md](docs/TESTING_PLAN.md) - Complete testing procedures\n- [docs/NIX_VS_SCRIPT_EVALUATION.md](docs/NIX_VS_SCRIPT_EVALUATION.md) - Evaluation framework\n- [docs/RESET_STRATEGY.md](docs/RESET_STRATEGY.md) - Detailed reset strategies\n- [docs/TOUCH_ID_SUDO_SETUP.md](docs/TOUCH_ID_SUDO_SETUP.md) - Touch ID configuration\n- [nixos-config/README.md](nixos-config/README.md) - Nix configuration guide\n\n## License\n\nMIT\n","numCharactersInRequestedRange":13061,"totalLinesInFile":493}

Lightweight browser automation\n- `Browser Use` - Browser interaction tools\n- `chrome-devtools` - Chrome debugging\n- `repomix` - Codebase analysis\n\n**Best for:** E2E testing, web scraping, browser automation\n\n## How It Works\n\n1. **Global Config** (`~/.cursor/mcp.json`): Minimal, always-on utilities (context7, repomix)\n2. **Project Config** (`.cursor/mcp.json`): Project-specific toolboxes activated as needed\n3. **Toolbox Library**: Pre-configured bundles in `cursor/mcp-toolboxes/`\n\nCursor prioritizes project-specific configs over global configs, so you get exactly what you need per project.\n\n## Usage Patterns\n\n### Starting a New Project\n```bash\ncd new-project\nactivate-mcp-toolbox web-dev\n# Restart Cursor\n```\n\n### Switching Context\n```bash\n# Working on cloud infrastructure now\nactivate-mcp-toolbox cloud-infra\n# Restart Cursor\n```\n\n### Creating Custom Toolboxes\n1. Copy an existing toolbox: `cp web-dev.json my-custom.json`\n2. Edit `my-custom.json` to add/remove MCPs\n3. Use it: `activate-mcp-toolbox my-custom`\n\n## Troubleshooting\n\n**Toolbox not found?**\n- Check available toolboxes: `activate-mcp-toolbox` (no args)\n- Toolboxes are in: `cursor/mcp-toolboxes/*.json`\n\n**MCPs not working after activation?**\n- Restart Cursor completely\n- Check `.cursor/mcp.json` exists in your project\n- Verify JSON syntax is valid\n\n**Want to disable MCPs for a project?**\n- Delete `.cursor/mcp.json` in the project\n- Or create an empty one: `echo '{\"mcpServers\":{}}' > .cursor/mcp.json`\n\n## Architecture\n\n```\n~/.cursor/mcp.json              # Global (minimal)\n  └─ context7, repomix\n\n.cursor/mcp.json                # Project-specific (toolbox)\n  └─ Selected MCPs from toolbox\n\ncursor/mcp-toolboxes/           # Toolbox definitions\n  ├─ web-dev.json\n  ├─ cloud-infra.json\n  └─ ...\n```\n\n## Best Practices\n\n1. **Start minimal**: Use `minimal` toolbox unless you need specific tools\n2. **One toolbox per project**: Don't mix toolboxes\n","originalContents":"- `Nanobrowser` - Lightweight browser automation\n- `Browser Use` - Browser interaction tools\n- `chrome-devtools` - Chrome debugging\n- `repomix` - Codebase analysis\n\n**Best for:** E2E testing, web scraping, browser automation\n\n## How It Works\n\n1. **Global Config** (`~/.cursor/mcp.json`): Minimal, always-on utilities (context7, repomix)\n2. **Project Config** (`.cursor/mcp.json`): Project-specific toolboxes activated as needed\n3. **Toolbox Library**: Pre-configured bundles in `cursor/mcp-toolboxes/`\n\nCursor prioritizes project-specific configs over global configs, so you get exactly what you need per project.\n\n## Usage Patterns\n\n### Starting a New Project\n```bash\ncd new-project\nactivate-mcp-toolbox web-dev\n# Restart Cursor\n```\n\n### Switching Context\n```bash\n# Working on cloud infrastructure now\nactivate-mcp-toolbox cloud-infra\n# Restart Cursor\n```\n\n### Creating Custom Toolboxes\n1. Anthropic Model Context Protocol (MCP) for Cursor\n\nThis document describes the Model Context Protocol setup for Cursor, which enables Claude to interact with external tools like GitHub.\n\n## What is MCP?\n\nThe Model Context Protocol (MCP) is Anthropic's protocol for connecting Claude with external tools and services. It allows Claude to:\n\n- Access and manipulate external data sources\n- Execute code and commands in controlled environments\n- Integrate with APIs and services\n- Work with files and repositories\n\n## GitHub MCP Server\n\nThe GitHub MCP server enables Claude to interact with GitHub repositories, providing capabilities like:\n\n- Creating or updating files in repositories\n- Pushing multiple files in a single commit\n- Searching repositories, code, issues, and users\n- Creating and managing issues and pull requests\n- Accessing file contents and repository information\n\n## Setup Instructions\n\n1. Make sure the MCP configuration is enabled in Cursor's settings.json:\n   ```json\n   \"cursor.experimental.anthropic.claude.modelContextProtocol\": true,\n   \"cursor.experimental.anthropic.claude.modelContextProtocolPath\": \"~/Library/Application Support/Cursor/User/mcp/config.json\"\n   ```\n\n2. Create a GitHub Personal Access Token (PAT) with appropriate permissions.\n\n3. Update the MCP configuration file with your token:\n   ```\n   ~/Library/Application Support/Cursor/User/mcp/config.json\n   ```\n   \n   Replace `YOUR_GITHUB_TOKEN` with your actual GitHub Personal Access Token.\n\n4. {"contents":"# MCP Layer Guide\n\nThis guide explains the layered MCP (Model Context Protocol) installation approach in toolchain-2026.\n\n## Overview\n\nFollowing toolchain-2026's layered architecture, MCP servers are organized into layers:\n\n1. **Base Layer** - Core MCP dependencies\n2. **AI Layer** - Cursor-specific MCP servers\n3. **Use-Case Layers** - Specialized MCP servers by use case\n\n## Layer Structure\n\n### Base Layer (`Brewfile.mcp-base`)\n\n**Purpose**: Core dependencies for MCP servers\n\n**Contents**:\n- Node.js (already in base layer)\n- Docker/OrbStack (in cloud layer, referenced here)\n- Documentation of MCP dependencies\n\n**Installation**:\n```bash\nbrew bundle --file=Brewfile.mcp-base\n```\n\n**Note**: Most MCP servers are installed via npm, Docker, or Python, not Homebrew.\n\n### AI Layer (`Brewfile.ai`)\n\n**Purpose**: AI-focused MCP servers for Cursor and other AI tools\n\n**Contents**:\n- Cursor-specific MCP servers\n- Repomix MCP server\n- AI-focused MCP tools\n\n**Installation**:\n```bash\nbrew bundle --file=Brewfile.ai\n./scripts/install-mcp-servers.sh --npm\n```\n\n### Use-Case Specific Layers\n\nMCP servers are organized by use case:\n\n#### Web Development\n- GitHub MCP\n- Filesystem MCP\n- Browser automation (Puppeteer MCP)\n\n#### Cloud/DevOps\n- Docker MCP\n- GCP MCP\n- Kubernetes MCP\n\n#### Data Science\n- SQLite MCP\n- Postgres MCP\n- Database access MCPs\n\n## Installation\n\n### Step 1: Install Base Dependencies\n\n```bash\n# Install base layer (includes Node.js)\n./install.sh --base\n\n# Install cloud layer (includes Docker/OrbStack)\n./install.sh --cloud\n```\n\n### Step 2: Install MCP Servers\n\n```bash\n# Install all MCP servers\n./scripts/install-mcp-servers.sh\n\n# Or install by method\n./scripts/install-mcp-servers.sh --npm\n./scripts/install-mcp-servers.sh --docker\n./scripts/install-mcp-servers.sh --python\n```\n\n### Step 3: Configure Cursor\n\n```bash\n# Setup global Cursor MCP config\n./scripts/setup-cursor-mcp.sh\n\n# Setup project-specific config\n./scripts/setup-cursor-mcp.sh --project\n```\n\n### Step 4: Verify Installation\n","numCharactersInRequestedRange":2007,"totalLinesInFile":208}

{"contents":"# Anthropic Model Context Protocol (MCP) for Cursor\n\nThis document describes the Model Context Protocol setup for Cursor, which enables Claude to interact with external tools like GitHub.\n\n## What is MCP?\n\nThe Model Context Protocol (MCP) is Anthropic's protocol for connecting Claude with external tools and services. It allows Claude to:\n\n- Access and manipulate external data sources\n- Execute code and commands in controlled environments\n- Integrate with APIs and services\n- Work with files and repositories\n\n## GitHub MCP Server\n\nThe GitHub MCP server enables Claude to interact with GitHub repositories, providing capabilities like:\n\n- Creating or updating files in repositories\n- Pushing multiple files in a single commit\n- Searching repositories, code, issues, and users\n- Creating and managing issues and pull requests\n- Accessing file contents and repository information\n\n## Setup Instructions\n\n1. Make sure the MCP configuration is enabled in Cursor's settings.json:\n   ```json\n   \"cursor.experimental.anthropic.claude.modelContextProtocol\": true,\n   \"cursor.experimental.anthropic.claude.modelContextProtocolPath\": \"~/Library/Application Support/Cursor/User/mcp/config.json\"\n   ```\n\n2. Create a GitHub Personal Access Token (PAT) with appropriate permissions.\n\n3. Update the MCP configuration file with your token:\n   ```\n   ~/Library/Application Support/Cursor/User/mcp/config.json\n   ```\n   \n   Replace `YOUR_GITHUB_TOKEN` with your actual GitHub Personal Access Token.\n\n4. Keep the MCP server package updated by running:\n   ```\n   ./scripts/update-mcp.sh\n   ```\n\n## Usage\n\nWhen you chat with Claude in Cursor, it can now access the GitHub MCP server to perform operations on GitHub repositories.\n\nExample commands:\n- \"Create a new file in my repository\"\n- \"Search for issues related to X\"\n- \"Update the README with new documentation\"\n- \"Create a pull request for these changes\"\n\n## Troubleshooting\n\n- If Claude can't access GitHub, check that your token has the necessary permissions.\n- Make sure the NPM package is installed: `npm list -g @modelcontextprotocol/server-github`\n- Check Cursor's logs for any MCP-related errors.\n\n## References\n\n- [Anthropic Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/)\n- [MCP GitHub Server Repository](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/servers/tree/main/src/github) ","numCharactersInRequestedRange":2332,"totalLinesInFile":65}

{"contents":"#!/usr/bin/env zsh\n\n# Script to dump Cursor workspace information to timestamped files\n# Extracts data from multiple sources for comprehensive state snapshot\n\n# Create timestamp\ntimestamp=$(date +%Y-%m-%d_%H-%M-%S)\n\n# Output directory (same as script location by default)\noutput_dir=\"${0:a:h}\"\nbase_name=\"cursor-workspace-${timestamp}\"\n\n# Output files\nstatus_file=\"${output_dir}/${base_name}.txt\"\njson_file=\"${output_dir}/${base_name}.json\"\n\necho \"📸 Creating Cursor workspace snapshot...\"\necho \"\"\n\n# 1. Get cursor status\necho \"[1/3] Getting cursor --status...\"\ncursor --status > \"${status_file}\"\n\n# 2. Extract structured data from status output and storage.json\necho \"[2/3] Extracting workspace data from storage and parsing windows...\"\nstorage_json=\"${HOME}/Library/Application Support/Cursor/User/globalStorage/storage.json\"\n\nif [[ -f \"$storage_json\" ]]; then\n    # Extract comprehensive workspace data using Python\n    python3 <<EOF > \"${json_file}\"\nimport json\nimport sys\nimport re\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\ntry:\n    # Read storage.json\n    with open('$storage_json', 'r') as f:\n        data = json.load(f)\n    \n    # Read status output to extract window details\n    with open('${status_file}', 'r') as f:\n        status_text = f.read()\n    \n    output = {\n        \"timestamp\": \"${timestamp}\",\n        \"windows\": [],\n        \"folders\": [],\n        \"recent_files\": [],\n        \"workspace_stats\": {}","numCharactersInRequestedRange":1402,"totalLinesInFile":184}

{"contents":"# MCP Toolbox System\n\nProject-specific MCP (Model Context Protocol) configuration toolboxes for Cursor. These are preassembled \"kits\" that provide exactly the tools you need for specific types of work, avoiding the performance issues that come from having too many MCPs enabled globally.\n\n## Quick Start\n\n```bash\ncd /path/to/your/project\nactivate-mcp-toolbox web-dev\n```\n\nThis creates `.cursor/mcp.json` in your project with the appropriate MCP servers enabled. **Restart Cursor** for changes to take effect.\n\n## Available Toolboxes\n\n### `minimal`\n**Use when:** You need basic utilities that work everywhere\n- `context7` - Documentation lookup\n- `repomix` - Codebase analysis\n\n**Best for:** Quick tasks, minimal overhead\n\n### `web-dev`\n**Use when:** Building web applications, frontend/backend development\n- `context7` - Documentation lookup\n- `repomix` - Codebase analysis\n- `chrome-devtools` - Browser debugging\n\n**Best for:** React, Vue, Next.js, web frameworks\n\n### `cloud-infra`\n**Use when:** Working with cloud infrastructure, deployments, DevOps\n- `gcloud` - Google Cloud Platform operations\n- `github` - GitHub repository management\n- `repomix` - Codebase analysis\n\n**Best for:** Terraform, Kubernetes, CI/CD, cloud deployments\n\n### `ai-research`\n**Use when:** AI/ML research, model exploration, data science\n- `context7` - Documentation lookup\n- `Hugging Face` - Model hub access\n- `hf-mcp-server` - Hugging Face integration\n- `Limitless` - AI research tools\n- `repomix` - Codebase analysis\n\n**Best for:** ML projects, model training, research papers\n\n### `full-stack`\n**Use when:** Complex projects requiring multiple integrations\n- `github` - Version control and collaboration\n- `Notion` - Documentation and knowledge management\n- `repomix` - Codebase analysis\n- `context7` - Documentation lookup\n- `gcloud` - Cloud operations\n\n**Best for:** Large projects, team collaboration, production systems\n\n### `browser-automation`\n**Use when:** Web scraping, browser testing, automation\n- `Nanobrowser` - Lightweight browser automation\n- `Browser Use` - Browser interaction tools\n- `chrome-devtools` - Chrome debugging\n- `repomix` - Codebase analysis\n\n**Best for:** E2E testing, web scraping, browser automation\n\n## How It Works\n\n1. **Global Config** (`~/.cursor/mcp.json`): Minimal, always-on utilities (context7, repomix)\n2. **Project Config** (`.cursor/mcp.json`): Project-specific toolboxes activated as needed\n3. **Toolbox Library**: Pre-configured bundles in `cursor/mcp-toolboxes/`\n\nCursor prioritizes project-specific configs over global configs, so you get exactly what you need per project.\n\n## Usage Patterns\n\n### Starting a New Project\n```bash\ncd new-project\nactivate-mcp-toolbox web-dev\n# Restart Cursor\n```\n\n### Switching Context\n```bash\n# Working on cloud infrastructure now\nactivate-mcp-toolbox cloud-infra\n# Restart Cursor\n```\n\n### Creating Custom Toolboxes\n1. Copy an existing toolbox: `cp web-dev.json my-custom.json`\n2. Edit `my-custom.json` to add/remove MCPs\n3. Use it: `activate-mcp-toolbox my-custom`\n\n## Troubleshooting\n\n**Toolbox not found?**\n- Check available toolboxes: `activate-mcp-toolbox` (no args)\n- Toolboxes are in: `cursor/mcp-toolboxes/*.json`\n\n**MCPs not working after activation?**\n- Restart Cursor completely\n- Check `.cursor/mcp.json` exists in your project\n- Verify JSON syntax is valid\n\n**Want to disable MCPs for a project?**\n- Delete `.cursor/mcp.json` in the project\n- Or create an empty one: `echo '{\"mcpServers\":{}}' > .cursor/mcp.json`\n\n## Architecture\n\n```\n~/.cursor/mcp.json              # Global (minimal)\n  └─ context7, repomix\n\n.cursor/mcp.json                # Project-specific (toolbox)\n  └─ Selected MCPs from toolbox\n\ncursor/mcp-toolboxes/           # Toolbox definitions\n  ├─ web-dev.json\n  ├─ cloud-infra.json\n  └─ ...\n```\n\n## Best Practices\n\n1. **Start minimal**: Use `minimal` toolbox unless you need specific tools\n2. **One toolbox per project**: Don't mix toolboxes\n3. **Restart after changes**: Cursor needs a restart to pick up MCP changes\n4. **Version control**: Commit `.cursor/mcp.json` to share toolbox choice with team\n5. **Custom toolboxes**: Create project-specific toolboxes for unique needs\n\n## Adding New Toolboxes\n\n1. Create a new JSON file in `cursor/mcp-toolboxes/`\n2. Follow the structure of existing toolboxes\n3. Document it in this README\n4. Test with `activate-mcp-toolbox <name>`\n\n## See Also\n\n- [MCP Documentation](https://modelcontextprotocol.info)\n- [Cursor MCP Setup](../README-mcp.md)\n- [SLOW Landscape Tracking](../../../tools/toolchain-2026/mcp-landscape/)\n","numCharactersInRequestedRange":4551,"totalLinesInFile":147}

{"contents":"#!/bin/bash\n\n# activate-mcp-toolbox.sh\n# Activates a pre-configured MCP toolbox for the current project\n#\n# Usage: activate-mcp-toolbox <toolbox-name>\n# Example: activate-mcp-toolbox web-dev\n\nset -e\n\n# Colors for output\nRED='\\033[0;31m'\nGREEN='\\033[0;32m'\nYELLOW='\\033[1;33m'\nBLUE='\\033[0;34m'\nNC='\\033[0m' # No Color\n\n# Get the directory where this script is located\nSCRIPT_DIR=\"$(cd \"$(dirname \"${BASH_SOURCE[0]}\")\" && pwd)\"\nTOOLBOX_DIR=\"$(dirname \"$SCRIPT_DIR\")/mcp-toolboxes\"\n\n# Check if toolbox name was provided\nif [ -z \"$1\" ]; then\n    echo -e \"${RED}Error: Toolbox name required${NC}\"\n    echo \"\"\n    echo \"Usage: activate-mcp-toolbox <toolbox-name>\"\n    echo \"\"\n    echo \"Available toolboxes:\"\n    ls -1 \"$TOOLBOX_DIR\"/*.json 2>/dev/null | sed 's|.*/||' | sed 's|\\.json$||' | sed 's|^|  - |' || echo \"  (none found)\"\n    exit 1\nfi\n\nTOOLBOX_NAME=\"$1\"\nTOOLBOX_FILE=\"$TOOLBOX_DIR/${TOOLBOX_NAME}.json\"\n\n# Check if toolbox exists\nif [ ! -f \"$TOOLBOX_FILE\" ]; then\n    echo -e \"${RED}Error: Toolbox '${TOOLBOX_NAME}' not found${NC}\"\n    echo \"\"\n    echo \"Available toolboxes:\"\n    ls -1 \"$TOOLBOX_DIR\"/*.json 2>/dev/null | sed 's|.*/||' | sed 's|\\.json$||' | sed 's|^|  - |' || echo \"  (none found)\"\n    exit 1\nfi\n\n# Check if we're in a git repository (common indicator of a project)\nif ! git rev-parse --git-dir > /dev/null 2>&1; then\n    echo -e \"${YELLOW}Warning: Not in a git repository. Proceeding anyway...${NC}\"\nfi\n\n# Create .cursor directory if it doesn't exist\nPROJECT_CURSOR_DIR=\".cursor\"\nif [ ! -d \"$PROJECT_CURSOR_DIR\" ]; then\n    mkdir -p \"$PROJECT_CURSOR_DIR\"\n    echo -e \"${BLUE}Created .cursor directory${NC}\"\nfi\n\n# Backup existing mcp.json if it exists\nPROJECT_MCP_FILE=\"$PROJECT_CURSOR_DIR/mcp.json\"\nif [ -f \"$PROJECT_MCP_FILE\" ]; then\n    BACKUP_FILE=\"${PROJECT_MCP_FILE}.backup.$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S)\"\n    cp \"$PROJECT_MCP_FILE\" \"$BACKUP_FILE\"\n    echo -e \"${BLUE}Backed up existing mcp.json to $(basename \"$BACKUP_FILE\")${NC}\"\nfi\n\n# Copy toolbox config to project\ncp \"$TOOLBOX_FILE\" \"$PROJECT_MCP_FILE\"\necho -e \"${GREEN}✓ Activated toolbox: ${TOOLBOX_NAME}${NC}\"\n\n# Validate JSON syntax\nif command -v jq > /dev/null 2>&1; then\n    if jq empty \"$PROJECT_MCP_FILE\" 2>/dev/null; then\n        echo -e \"${GREEN}✓ JSON syntax validated${NC}\"\n    else\n        echo -e \"${RED}✗ Warning: JSON syntax validation failed${NC}\"\n        exit 1\n    fi\nfi\n\n# List activated MCPs\necho \"\"\necho -e \"${BLUE}Activated MCP servers:${NC}\"\nif command -v jq > /dev/null 2>&1; then\n    jq -r '.mcpServers | keys[]' \"$PROJECT_MCP_FILE\" | sed 's/^/  - /'\nelse\n    grep -o '\"[^\"]*\":' \"$PROJECT_MCP_FILE\" | sed 's/\":$//' | sed 's/^\"//' | sed 's/^/  - /'\nfi\n\necho \"\"\necho -e \"${YELLOW}Note: Restart Cursor for changes to take effect${NC}\"\n","numCharactersInRequestedRange":2733,"totalLinesInFile":90}

{"contents":"# MCP Layer Guide\n\nThis guide explains the layered MCP (Model Context Protocol) installation approach in toolchain-2026.\n\n## Overview\n\nFollowing toolchain-2026's layered architecture, MCP servers are organized into layers:\n\n1. **Base Layer** - Core MCP dependencies\n2. **AI Layer** - Cursor-specific MCP servers\n3. **Use-Case Layers** - Specialized MCP servers by use case\n\n## Layer Structure\n\n### Base Layer (`Brewfile.mcp-base`)\n\n**Purpose**: Core dependencies for MCP servers\n\n**Contents**:\n- Node.js (already in base layer)\n- Docker/OrbStack (in cloud layer, referenced here)\n- Documentation of MCP dependencies\n\n**Installation**:\n```bash\nbrew bundle --file=Brewfile.mcp-base\n```\n\n**Note**: Most MCP servers are installed via npm, Docker, or Python, not Homebrew.\n\n### AI Layer (`Brewfile.ai`)\n\n**Purpose**: AI-focused MCP servers for Cursor and other AI tools\n\n**Contents**:\n- Cursor-specific MCP servers\n- Repomix MCP server\n- AI-focused MCP tools\n\n**Installation**:\n```bash\nbrew bundle --file=Brewfile.ai\n./scripts/install-mcp-servers.sh --npm\n```\n\n### Use-Case Specific Layers\n\nMCP servers are organized by use case:\n\n#### Web Development\n- GitHub MCP\n- Filesystem MCP\n- Browser automation (Puppeteer MCP)\n\n#### Cloud/DevOps\n- Docker MCP\n- GCP MCP\n- Kubernetes MCP\n\n#### Data Science\n- SQLite MCP\n- Postgres MCP\n- Database access MCPs\n\n## Installation\n\n### Step 1: Install Base Dependencies\n\n```bash\n# Install base layer (includes Node.js)\n./install.sh --base\n\n# Install cloud layer (includes Docker/OrbStack)\n./install.sh --cloud\n```\n\n### Step 2: Install MCP Servers\n\n```bash\n# Install all MCP servers\n./scripts/install-mcp-servers.sh\n\n# Or install by method\n./scripts/install-mcp-servers.sh --npm\n./scripts/install-mcp-servers.sh --docker\n./scripts/install-mcp-servers.sh --python\n```\n\n### Step 3: Configure Cursor\n\n```bash\n# Setup global Cursor MCP config\n./scripts/setup-cursor-mcp.sh\n\n# Setup project-specific config\n./scripts/setup-cursor-mcp.sh --project\n```\n\n### Step 4: Verify Installation\n\n```bash\n# Check MCP server health\n./scripts/mcp-health-check.sh\n\n# List configured servers\n./scripts/mcp-manager.sh list\n```\n\n## Configuration Management\n\n### Global Configuration\n\nLocation: `~/.cursor/mcp.json`\n\nContains:\n- Common MCP servers (filesystem, GitHub)\n- User-specific configurations\n- Shared across all projects\n\n### Project Configuration\n\nLocation: `.cursor/mcp.json` `mcp/mcp-config.json`:\n\n- **minimal**: Essential servers only\n- **standard**: General development\n- **full**: All available servers\n- **docker**: Docker-based servers only\n\n## Use Case {"contents":"# macOS 2026 Toolchain\n\nA Spacemacs-style layered approach to reproducible macOS development environment configuration.\n\n## Quick Start\n\n### Bootstrap from GitHub (No Git Required)\n\nOn a fresh macOS system where git isn't available yet (git requires Xcode Command Line Tools), you can bootstrap directly from GitHub using curl:\n\n```bash\n# Download and run bootstrap script (recommended - safer)\ncurl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aculich/toolchain-2026/main/bootstrap.sh -o /tmp/bootstrap.sh && chmod +x /tmp/bootstrap.sh && /tmp/bootstrap.sh\n```\n\nOr as a one-liner (pipes directly to bash):\n\n```bash\ncurl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aculich/toolchain-2026/main/bootstrap.sh | bash\n```\n\n**Note**: This is useful for fresh macOS installations where git isn't installed yet. After bootstrap completes, you'll have git and can clone the repository normally.\n\n### Standard Quick Start (Git Already Available)\n\nIf you already have git installed:\n\n```bash\n# Clone the repository\ngit clone https://github.com/aculich/toolchain-2026.git\ncd toolchain-2026\n\n# Quick start with script-based (default)\n./bootstrap.sh\n./install.sh --base\n\n# Or choose Nix-based installation\n./bootstrap.sh --install-method nix\ncd nixos-config && ./install-lix-complete.sh\n\n# Or choose Pixi-based installation (fastest, best for data science)\n./bootstrap.sh --install-method pixi\n./install-pixi.sh --base --data\n\n# Install base + AI development\n./install.sh --base --ai\n\n# Install everything\n./install.sh --all\n\n# See all options\n./install.sh --help\n```\n\n**Note**: Three installation approaches are available:\n- **Script-based** (default): Homebrew-based, fast, native macOS integration\n- **Nix-based**: Fully declarative, reproducible, system configuration\n- **Pixi-based** (new): Fastest setup, excellent for data science, hybrid approach\n\nSee [docs/PIXI_VS_SCRIPT_VS_NIX.md](docs/PIXI_VS_SCRIPT_VS_NIX.md) for comparison. Decision deadline: Mid-February 2026.\n\n## Hard Reset (Fresh Start)\n\n**Purpose**: Remove Nix partition and user data to start completely fresh without reinstalling macOS.\n\n**What gets removed**:\n- Nix store (`/nix`)\n- User home directory contents\n- Homebrew packages (if desired)\n- All local repositories\n\n**What's preserved**: macOS installation, system files, other user accounts\n\n### Hard Reset Process\n\n1. **Remove Nix Installation** (if installed):\n   ```bash\n   # If installed with Lix\n   /nix/nix-installer uninstall\n   \n   # Or manually remove Nix\n   sudo rm -rf /nix\n   sudo rm -rf /etc/nix\n   sudo rm -rf ~/.config/nix\n   sudo rm -rf ~/.nix-profile\n   sudo rm -rf ~/.nix-defexpr\n   # Remove Nix references from shell profiles (~/.zshrc, ~/.bash_profile)\n   ```\n\n2. **Remove User Data** (choose one method):\n   - **Method A - Recovery Mode** (most thorough):\n     - Boot to Recovery Mode (Apple Silicon: hold power; Intel: Cmd+R)\n     - Open Terminal\n     - `rm -rf /Users/username/*`\n     - Reboot\n   - **Method B - Multi-User** (recommended for frequent resets):\n     - Log into another admin account\n     - Delete user account via System Preferences\n     - Recreate user account\n\n3. **Clean Up Homebrew** (optional):\n   ```bash\n   /bin/bash -c \"$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Homebrew/install/HEAD/uninstall.sh)\"\n   ```\n\n## Complete Setup from Scratch\n\nAfter a hard reset or on a fresh macOS installation, follow these steps to set up your development environment.\n\n### Phase 1: Clone Repository\n\n```bash\ncd ~\ngit clone https://github.com/aculich/toolchain-2026.git\ncd toolchain-2026\n```\n\n### Phase 2: Bootstrap\n\n```bash\n./bootstrap.sh\n# Or choose installation method:\n./bootstrap.sh --install-method nix    # Use Nix-based\n./bootstrap.sh --install-method script # Use script-based (default)\n./bootstrap.sh --install-method ask   # Interactive choice\n\n# If interrupted, resume from checkpoint:\n./bootstrap.sh --resume\n```\n\n**What bootstrap installs**:\n- Xcode Command Line Tools\n- Homebrew\n- bash 4+, git, GNU tools\n- Cursor, 1Password CLI, llm CLI\n\n**New features** (2026-01-04):\n- **Comprehensive logging** - All operations logged with timestamps\n- **Checkpoint system** - Resume from any checkpoint with `--resume`\n- **Early Touch ID setup** - Enables Touch ID for sudo before any sudo operations\n- **Enhanced 1Password setup** - Interactive guide with guard system\n- **Sentinel monitoring** - Real-time monitoring with error detection\n- **Progress reporting** - Visual progress bars and step announcements\n\n**Manual steps during bootstrap**:\n1. Install Xcode Command Line Tools (if prompted)\n2. Sign in to 1Password CLI: `op signin`\n\n### Phase 3: Configure 1Password\n","numCharactersInRequestedRange":4614,"totalLinesInFile":493}

MISSING\"\n    fi\n}\n\necho \"Checking Cursor configuration symlinks...\"\necho \"\"\n\ncheck_symlink \"$HOME/Library/Application Support/Cursor/User/settings.json\" \"Settings\"\ncheck_symlink \"$HOME/Library/Application Support/Cursor/User/keybindings.json\" \"Keybindings\"\ncheck_symlink \"$HOME/.cursor/mcp.json\" \"MCP Config\"\ncheck_symlink \"$HOME/.cursor/hooks.json\" \"Hooks\"\ncheck_symlink \"$HOME/.cursor/rules\" \"Rules\"\ncheck_symlink \"$HOME/.cursor/hooks_blueplane\" \"Hooks Blueplane\"\ncheck_symlink \"$HOME/dotfiles/cursor/ApplicationSupport\" \"ApplicationSupport\"\n```\n\n## Symlink Maintenance\n\n### Regular Tasks\n\n1. **Monthly Validation**: Run validation script to check for broken symlinks\n2. **After Updates**: Verify symlinks after Cursor updates\n3. **Before Changes**: Backup before modifying symlink strategy\n4. **Cross-Machine Sync**: Ensure dotfiles are synced before creating symlinks on new machine\n\n### Troubleshooting\n\n#### Broken Symlink\n\n**Symptom**: Symlink exists but target is missing\n\n**Solution**:\n```bash\n# Remove broken symlink\nrm ~/.cursor/mcp.json\n\n# Recreate if file exists in dotfiles\nln -s ~/dotfiles/cursor/mcp.json ~/.cursor/mcp.json\n```\n\n#### File Exists (Not Symlink)\n\n**Symptom**: File exists but is not a symlink\n\n**Solution**:\n```bash\n# Backup existing file\ncp ~/.cursor/mcp.json ~/.cursor/mcp.json.backup\n\n# Remove and create symlink\nrm ~/.cursor/mcp.json\nln -s ~/dotfiles/cursor/mcp.json ~/.cursor/mcp.json\n```\n\n#### Target Missing\n\n**Symptom**: Symlink points to non-existent file\n\n**Solution**:\n```bash\n# Check if file exists in dotfiles\nls -la ~/dotfiles/cursor/mcp.json\n\n# If missing, copy from live (if exists)\nif [ -f ~/.cursor/mcp.json ] && [ ! -f ~/dotfiles/cursor/mcp.json ]; then\n    cp ~/.cursor/mcp.json ~/dotfiles/cursor/mcp.json\n    git add ~/dotfiles/cursor/mcp.json\nfi\n```\n\n## Integration with Dotfile Managers\n\n### GNU Stow\n\nIf using GNU Stow for dotfile management:\n\n```bash\n# Stow cursor configs\nstow -d ~/dotfiles -t ~ cursor\n\n# This would create symlinks for all files in ~/dotfiles/cursor\n```\n\n### Manual Management\n\nCurrent approach uses manual symlink creation, which provides:\n- Explicit control over what gets symlinked\n- Clear documentation of symlink strategy\n- Easy troubleshooting\n\n## Best Practices\n\n1. **Always Backup**: Backup existing files before creating symlinks\n2. **Verify Targets**: Ensure dotfiles exist before creating symlinks\n3. **Document Changes**: Update this document when adding new symlinks\n4. **Test After Changes**: Validate symlinks after any changes\n5. **Version Control**: Commit symlink strategy changes to git\n\n## Summary\n\n### Current Status\n\n✅ **Active Symlinks**:\n- `settings.json` → dotfiles\n- `keybindings.json` → dotfiles\n- `ApplicationSupport` → User directory\n\n⏳ **Pending Symlinks**:\n- `mcp.json` (High priority)\n- `hooks.json` (Medium priority)\n- `rules/` (Medium priority)\n- `hooks_blueplane/` (Medium priority)\n- `cli-config.json` (Low priority)\n\n❌ **Never Symlink**:\n- Runtime data (chats, projects, plans, logs)\n- Installed extensions\n- Local git repository\n\n### Next Steps\n\n1. Create symlink management script\n2. Create symlinks for pending configurations\n3. Set up validation script\n4. Document in dotfiles repository\n5. Test on secondary machine (sidequest)\n"}
